interfaces: ControlledMergeResult { taskId, lifecycleState: 'DONE', pullRequestNumber, sourceRevision, mergeCommitSha, evidenceLineageId, evidenceSequence }

ControlledMergeErrorCode = INVALID_REQUEST | TASK_NOT_FOUND | TASK_STATE_NOT_MERGEABLE | BRANCH_REJECTED | NOT_MERGE_READY | HEAD_CHANGED | MERGE_PROVIDER_FAILED | MERGE_NOT_CONFIRMED | EVIDENCE_REJECTED | LIFECYCLE_REJECTED | LOCK_RELEASE_FAILED | STATE_CONFLICT | STATE_IO_FAILED
ControlledMergeReadinessPort.evaluate({ taskId }): Promise<EvaluateMergeReadinessResult> boundary onto control-plane.merge-readiness
ControlledMergePullRequestPort.findPullRequestByHead(head): Promise<ControlledMergePullRequestRecord | null>, any pull-request state, most recent by creation date
ControlledMergePullRequestRecord { number, headSha, baseRef, state, merged, mergeCommitSha }
ControlledMergeTaskLock.withLock<T>(taskId, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>, an async-critical-section variant of BOOT-018's/BOOT-019's/BOOT-020's/BOOT-021's own synchronous task-lock port
FileControlledMergeTaskLock(root) concrete ControlledMergeTaskLock over .agent/state/lifecycle/<taskId>.lifecycle.lock, sharing the lifecycle root FileControlledMergeStateStore uses
GitHubControlledMergePullRequestOperations(options) concrete ControlledMergePullRequestPort adapter over the GitHub REST pulls/merge endpoints

behavioralConstraints: merge() acquires an exclusive per-task lock (ControlledMergeTaskLock.withLock) around its entire read-decide-write critical section — including every awaited branch/readiness/provider call — before doing anything else, so two concurrent merge() calls for the same task never interleave; a concurrent call finds the lock held and is rejected as STATE_CONFLICT

merge() only ever acts on a task whose persisted lifecycle currentState is MERGE_READY, MERGED, or DONE; any other state is rejected as TASK_STATE_NOT_MERGEABLE before any branch, readiness, or provider call

a task already DONE returns its persisted ipt.merge-evidence record (read through control-plane.evidence-store's mergeEvidenceLineageId(taskId)) unchanged, with no branch, readiness, provider, lock, or lifecycle-state write of any kind

immediately after resolving the task's lifecycle record (for any non-DONE entry state), the assignment lock's exact identity (lockId) is captured once via ControlledMergeLockStore.get(); this captured identity, never a freshly re-read lock, is what completion later attempts to release

a task already MERGED (a prior call wrote merge evidence and the MERGED lifecycle transition but was interrupted before lock release/DONE) resumes purely from its persisted merge evidence: no branch check, no merge-readiness evaluation, and no pull-request provider call of any kind runs on this path

for a task in MERGE_READY, the canonical branch and exact current revision are resolved strictly through the unmodified control-plane.git-branch-lifecycle adapter; a Git branch mismatch or Git failure (including a failure resolving the revision itself) is normalized to BRANCH_REJECTED before any other check

before evaluating merge readiness, the canonical branch's pull request (any state, not only open) is looked up once; it is trusted as a confirmed prior result — skipping merge-readiness evaluation and the mergePullRequest call entirely — only when it already reports merged=true AND the task's own lifecycle history still binds its MERGE_READY transition to the exact current revision AND its base matches the configured integrationTarget (default 'main'); when merged=true but either the revision binding or the base check fails, the shortcut is not taken and control falls through to the normal readiness-evaluate path, which safely rejects (the merged/closed PR is invisible to findOpenPullRequests, so evaluate() reports PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND) rather than trusting a stale binding or a PR merged into the wrong base

when the pull request is not already merged (or the already-merged shortcut's gating fails), control-plane.merge-readiness's evaluate() is invoked for the exact task; its own resolved revision is compared against the revision this controller already resolved, and any mismatch is rejected as HEAD_CHANGED before ready is even inspected
a ready=false merge-readiness result is rejected as NOT_MERGE_READY, carrying every reason's message; mergePullRequest is never called in this case

immediately before calling mergePullRequest, the pull request is looked up one more time; any change in its number, head SHA, or merged status relative to the merge-readiness result already evaluated is rejected as HEAD_CHANGED without calling the merge provider

mergePullRequest is called with the exact expected head SHA; a real GitHub adapter passes it as the merge endpoint's own sha parameter, so a head that moved between this controller's last local check and GitHub's own processing of the request is rejected server-side (HTTP 409) and mapped to HEAD_CHANGED here, never silently merging a different commit
a mergePullRequest response reporting merged=false is rejected as MERGE_NOT_CONFIRMED; no evidence is recorded and no lifecycle transition occurs, leaving the task MERGE_READY and safe to retry

a provider failure (network, HTTP, or malformed response) while finding or merging a pull request is normalized to MERGE_PROVIDER_FAILED (or, for GitHub's own 409 head-mismatch response, to HEAD_CHANGED) and leaves the task's persisted lifecycle state and evidence completely unchanged

only once a merge is confirmed (either freshly, or already-merged and read back) is exactly one ipt.merge-evidence record written, naming the task, the merged source revision, the pull-request number, the merge commit SHA, and a policyDecisionReference string; this record is written before the MERGE_READY -> MERGED lifecycle transition, so that transition's own evidenceRef always names an already-persisted record

the assignment lock is released only as a best-effort, idempotent step after the MERGED transition persists, and only ever targets the exact lockId captured at entry: if the currently active lock (re-read at release time) is missing or its lockId no longer matches the captured one — because it was released already, or reassigned to a different actor's legitimate assignment while this call was in flight — release() is never called at all, and no error is raised; only when the captured lockId is still the exact active lock is release() invoked, and only then does a rejection other than LOCK_NOT_FOUND/LOCK_ID_MISMATCH surface as LOCK_RELEASE_FAILED, which blocks the MERGED -> DONE transition but leaves the already-persisted MERGED state and evidence fully resumable on a later call
the MERGED -> DONE transition is attempted only after lock release succeeds or is treated as already-handled; a rejected DONE transition is surfaced as LIFECYCLE_REJECTED

DONE is reachable through this module only by way of a confirmed merge result feeding a persisted merge-evidence record feeding the MERGE_READY -> MERGED -> DONE lifecycle transitions; there is no path that reaches DONE from any other evidence or from a caller-supplied override
invariants: this is the only module the bootstrap defines that transitions a task through MERGED or to DONE; no other module writes either state

merge() never calls the merge provider more than once for the same confirmed merge: a resume after any interruption point either finds the pull request already merged (via findPullRequestByHead) or reads back already-persisted merge evidence, never re-invoking mergePullRequest
merge() never records merge evidence or writes a lifecycle transition for a merge that failed, was rejected, or was not confirmed by the provider

task-domain logic (ControlledMergeController) depends only on its typed dependency-port interfaces; it never inspects GitHub-specific response shapes or another module's internal storage layout directly

a branch, evidence, lifecycle, lock, or provider failure that occurs before a merge is confirmed always leaves the task's persisted lifecycle state exactly as it was found, so every such failure is safely retryable

completion never releases an assignment lock other than the exact lockId observed at the start of the same merge() call; a lock reassigned to a different actor while a call is in flight is never released by that call
examples: a MERGE_READY task whose merge-readiness evaluate() reports ready=true, whose pull request is still open and unmerged at the approved revision on both the initial and immediate pre-merge checks, and whose merge provider confirms merged=true transitions MERGE_READY -> MERGED -> DONE, with one ipt.merge-evidence record naming the merge commit SHA
a MERGE_READY task whose merge-readiness evaluate() reports ready=false is rejected as NOT_MERGE_READY without ever calling the merge provider, and the task remains MERGE_READY
a MERGE_READY task whose pull request's head changes between the merge-readiness evaluation and the immediate pre-merge recheck is rejected as HEAD_CHANGED without calling the merge provider

a MERGE_READY task whose pull request is discovered already merged=true (a previous call's merge provider call succeeded but this controller crashed before recording evidence), whose lifecycle history still binds MERGE_READY to the exact current revision, and whose merged PR's base matches the configured integration target is finalized directly from that confirmed result — no merge-readiness evaluation and no second mergePullRequest call occur

a MERGE_READY task whose pull request is discovered already merged=true but whose lifecycle history does NOT bind MERGE_READY to the exact current revision (or whose merged PR targeted the wrong base) is not trusted via the shortcut; evaluate() is called normally and safely reports PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND/NOT_MERGE_READY instead
a MERGED task (evidence and the MERGED transition already persisted, but lock release/DONE was interrupted) resumes purely from its persisted evidence with zero pull-request provider calls
a DONE task returns its persisted evidence unchanged on every subsequent call, with zero branch, provider, lock, or state-store writes
a merge provider call that fails outright (network error, non-2xx response) leaves the task MERGE_READY with no evidence recorded, safely retryable
an assignment lock already released by an earlier, successful completion attempt does not cause a later idempotent DONE-path call to fail
an assignment lock reassigned to a different actor's legitimate assignment between this call's entry and its completion step is left untouched: release() is never invoked for it
a second merge() call for the same task while the first is still in its critical section is rejected as STATE_CONFLICT by the task lock rather than interleaving with the first
edgeCases: an unregistered taskId is rejected as TASK_NOT_FOUND
a non-schema-valid taskId, or an empty/untrimmed actorId, runId, or occurredAt, is rejected as INVALID_REQUEST before any dependency is touched
a task in any lifecycle state other than MERGE_READY, MERGED, or DONE (for example IN_DEVELOPMENT or QA_REVIEW) is rejected as TASK_STATE_NOT_MERGEABLE
a Git branch mismatch reported by the branch adapter is normalized to BRANCH_REJECTED rather than propagating a raw BranchLifecycleError
a merge-readiness evaluate() call that itself throws is normalized to MERGE_PROVIDER_FAILED
a merge-readiness result whose own resolved revision differs from the revision this controller already resolved is rejected as HEAD_CHANGED before ready is inspected
a confirmed already-merged pull request whose head SHA does not match the approved revision is rejected as HEAD_CHANGED rather than finalized against an unapproved commit
a confirmed already-merged pull request reporting merged=true with no merge commit SHA is rejected as MERGE_NOT_CONFIRMED

a MERGED task with no persisted merge evidence at all (a state this module's own writes never produce, since evidence is always recorded before the MERGED transition persists) is rejected as EVIDENCE_REJECTED rather than silently completing without an audit trail
rejected merge evidence (a schema-validation failure) is surfaced as EVIDENCE_REJECTED and blocks the lifecycle transition entirely
a lock-release rejection other than LOCK_NOT_FOUND/LOCK_ID_MISMATCH is surfaced as LOCK_RELEASE_FAILED, which still leaves the already-persisted MERGED state and evidence resumable

a non-strictly-RFC-3339 occurredAt (for example missing a timezone offset/Z) is rejected as INVALID_REQUEST before any branch, readiness, or provider call — never discovered only later when the stricter evidence-schema check rejects it after an irreversible merge already happened

GitHub's list-pull-requests response (used by findPullRequestByHead) exposes merged_at, not the merged boolean the single-pull-request endpoint returns; merged is derived as merged_at !== null so a real list-endpoint result is never rejected as malformed

a stale controlled-merge task-lock file (older than the same 5-minute threshold BOOT-018's/BOOT-019's/BOOT-020's/BOOT-021's own task locks use) is reclaimed by the next caller rather than wedging the task indefinitely if a prior holder crashed mid-merge

expectations: BOOT-026+ can drive a MERGE_READY task to DONE by calling merge() once per attempt, trusting NOT_MERGE_READY/HEAD_CHANGED/MERGE_PROVIDER_FAILED/MERGE_NOT_CONFIRMED as exact, safely-retryable reasons a call did not reach DONE, without the orchestrator itself needing to re-derive merge readiness, re-check the pull request head, or track whether a prior attempt already merged
acceptedRanges: a ControlledMergeResult with lifecycleState 'DONE' for a task that was MERGE_READY, MERGED, or DONE on entry
a thrown ControlledMergeError whose code and recoverable flag say whether retrying merge() unchanged can succeed
requiredReachableRanges: DONE is reachable for a task whose merge-readiness genuinely holds and whose pull request genuinely merges

every non-DONE outcome leaves the task's persisted lifecycle state unchanged from what merge() observed on entry, except a lock-release failure, which leaves it at MERGED with evidence already persisted
